reviews.title: What Happened to this APP??
reviews.text: The Trip Planner has gotten horrible! Every time you close a location (campground or other, it closes everything you are working on and takes you back to the home page. The GPS has gone from 99%reliable to probably 60%. One example - recently when leaving Holbrook AZ headed to Monument Valley, it had us get off at a questionable off ramp. I should have followed my gut but I followed the GPS. The road was grown over with weeds. I untidy lines truck happened up shortly after getting on the road and told us to tern around. The road was closed. We had to disconnect our tow vehicle and back up about 50 yards and make a K turn in our Class A. That was the worst but there were other very questionable routings to where we started using Waze and an atlas. Also, now while planning a trip, the ICONS are up in the corner - you only have a quarter screen, and like I said, every time you close one screen it takes you back to the home page. It SUCKS.

reviews.title: Not impressed
reviews.text: We used this app for the first time for navigation. I really wanted an app that would take into consideration our camper height for bridges and underpasses. We were ok there, but the app tried to take us down a road that had NO OUTLET marked and also down a road that would have just U turned us. I happened to know the area so I knew not to follow the directions. That's NOT cool. The voice is also very drab and the highlighted roadway is too small to reality see a difference between where it wants you to drive versus just the regular road. The app came very recommended but I can't say I'm impressed at all. Disappointed.

reviews.title: Nightmare routing!
reviews.text:
We were traveling on I-40 East from Nashville to Fancy Gap, VA. RVLife routes us off  and took us down a very dangerous route with no way to abort or turn around. Crazy tight switchback corners, low clearance , and literally impossible for 2 rigs to have passed in opposite directions. Thankfully, we only had to navigate around a trash truck. But even that was by LESS than an inch. Lesson learned, not trusting this RV routing software again. I wish I had been able to make note of the route, but I was too busy. 

Why bother putting in all our rig specs if you're routes down a road barely fit for a sports car!

reviews.title: Expensively Useless
reviews.text:
I reviewed the settings and preferences available for RV Life and it all sounded great and safe. It is NOT. The mapping and trip progress tracking is AWFUL, and even though the app records details of your vehicle and rig/camper- it DOES NOT route a safe map. My 5th wheel is 13 ft 8 inches tall and this app planner a route for me traveling under a notoriously well known 13’ 6” overpass. 
It has tried to route me to travel down Forest Service roads that aren’t meant for public use, and that would require me to dive across an open field to reach a destination. 
Also- be prepared for TONS of spam and unwanted “sponsored” emails and messages. I’m canceling and requesting a refund- though I’m sure I’ll never get it.

reviews.title: Great, extremely useful App, but…

reviews.title: DANGEROUS UPDATE
reviews.text:
Recent update requires acknowledging some legal BS before merging to the map for driving.  When the app/iPhone/radio etc reboots or disconnects during a drive the map will not cube back up until you acknowledge the legal BS on the iPhone.  Can’t legally do that driving in most states, and even if you could it’s dangerous leaving the only option to use another machination app that doesn’t consider RV limitations or stop driving to get out worked out.

Time to find another app of this isn’t fixed in a week.

reviews.title: Overall Disappointing

With today’s technology, I just don’t understand the logic and feedback of the system and it is getting worse.  I fulltime in a 39’ 5th wheel and to be ask to make u-turns and travel thru city neighborhoods is unacceptable!!!

reviews.title: Hard to enter trips
reviews.text: First time user and I named a trip trying to use my current starting location. I had to turn permission on in my phone for it to use location ( understandable), came back to the app and had to start over. Tried naming the trip with the same name and it showed the trip already existed. I checked trips, planned trips , and archived trips and it didn’t show anywhere. I tried to enter twice more with a new name and although permissions wer on, the app continued to say permissions were not on. I gave up. It could be a great app, who knows?

reviews.title: Not intuitive

reviews.title: So Many Issues
reviews.text: Where do I begin? How about telling me to get off - trailer in tow - at exit 119 south on I-41 in Wisconsin just to get right back on? How about that I picked a route from Door County to Rockford through Madison, not Milwaukee, but this stupid app changed back to Milwaukee without my approval? How about the fact that the default zoom level is way too zoomed in and YOU CANT CHANGE IT.? How about that it lowers your music volume to speak and then doesn’t turn it back up for 15-30 min so you’re blasted with loud music randomly? How about that it tells you to “keep left” to stay on 90 W at 94 north of Madison (going south) when keeping left will take you on 94 (wrong verbal directions are a constant problem)? How about telling you to turn into Airstream of Chicago in Naperville through an exit only drive that is facing the opposite direction? I could go on and on, but this is the worst, most frustrating GPS app ever created.

reviews.title: Piece of trash and dangerous
reviews.text:
Let’s talk pros. I love the review, tips of places. 

Now negatives. I used the GPS paid version this weekend. During the set up I made sure to avoid a highway that everyone said was not safe in a trailer.  However the program kept changing to the dangerous route.  On the way going it added an extra hour to my route as I tried to find the right route.   Even coming home I had to redo the directions multiple times.  

With CarPlay you can’t move in or out, the computer voice doesn’t shut up and is so annoying you want to scream.  The only way to turn it I off is closing the program on your phone.  

I’ll use the free version of this to read and write reviews.  But personally I consider the GPS portion to be extremely frustrating, annoying and dangerous to use in my opinion

reviews.title: App not ready for prime PAID use
reviews.text:
This app would be ok back in 2000s, but 25 years later one would expect more, especially for paid service. Here is a list of features all other FREE GPS apps have.
Live traffic data updates with option to seek alternative routes.
Option to seek POI while road guidance is active.
While in active GPS route, no option to zoom in or out (other than pinch) or set zoom, no potion to rotate map north or drive north. 
Route feedback is limited to only few obstacles.
Once route is active, no option to switch to other menus.
Creating trips requires separate web based site and is counter intuitive it makes you wanna cry. Once you create trips, editing starting point or adding POI isn’t available. 
Mobile internet site will not access GPS to select starting point for the trip.
The list of missing basic GPS navigation tools is so long that they should pay me to use it instead. 
So safe your money and find something else. 
To the developers, I have low expectations of you reading it and implementing the missing features as it would require you to rewrite this app from the beginning. Instead you pray on suckers like me to subscribe (for a one month).

reviews.title: Questionable RV routes
reviews.text: I bought rv life because I needed an rv gps for our new to us Tiffin. It is a taller rv than we are used to and wanted to make sure we were taking the safest routes. We used it in conjunction with Apple Maps and Google Maps. We are planning on getting the garmin gps unit, but didn’t have time before our two week trip. We thought rv life would suffice for one trip. Boy were we wrong! It took us down winding one lane roads, narrow roads not wide enough for an rv, and many many roads with low hanging trees. It was constantly taking us in different routes than the other two maps and when we followed the rv life route, we ended up on the wrong kinds of roads. Following the other routes were way more helpful. The only thing rv life did was make sure there were no low bridges on our route. The app seems to think that as long as a road doesn’t have a low bridge, it must be safe for an rv. A one land road exactly paved exactly 8’ wide with a cliff on one side and nowhere to go if another vehicle of any kind comes from the opposite direction is not my idea of a safe rv road. The other thing that was incredibly annoying about this app is that when we were out of cell range, it wouldn’t load the maps even though I downloaded all the maps I needed. It would tell me it couldn’t load a route because I needed to have the map downloaded when I was offline even though I’d go to the map and it wears already downloaded. How is that helpful? The whole reason I made sure to download the maps is be

reviews.title: Check with Google Maps before trusting RV Life navigation
reviews.text: We’re on a cross country trip. The first 5 weeks we only used RV Life Trip Wizard navigation. We never had a problem until driving from Sparks, GA to  Smokemont Campground, Great Smoky Mountains NP. RV Life Navigation had us turn East on Hwy 74 for 13 miles then turn left onto the Blue Ridge Mountain Parkway. As we came to realize, this parkway was steep, winding, low hanging trees, etc for ~20 miles. After arriving at our campground and speaking with the host, we should have driven only 6.6 miles on 441 N from Cherokee NC to Smokemont. From now on we use Google Maps and add “ask a question” for driving with a 30’ travel trailer and only use RV Life navigation as a simple guide.

reviews.title: Frustrating Experience
reviews.text: I used it this past weekend and was very frustrating. I had to switch back to Google maps and my Ford Trucks navigation  app. I like to know when my next turn is so I give myself plenty of time to get in the proper lane. On the RV Life app it seems to have these left and right angled arrows listed in the detail directions but it's just the flow of the road. No turning is necessary. I went into the left lane thinking I needed to turn left based on these detailed arrows and then a few minutes later it's telling me to turn right. It also sometimes thinks that I'm off on the off ramp and tells me directions to get on the main road that I'm already on. You have to constantly check the screen when you hear directions to make sure it has you on the right road.

reviews.title: What’s the point?
reviews.text: I’ve made one 5 legged trip with this app. I have the settings set for animal friendly, pull through camping. The app still shows campgrounds/RV parks that don’t have pull through sites and some that aren’t pet friendly. Each leg you have to reset whether you want main highways or not. The GPS is weird, I pulled off for fuel and to let my dog do business and the GPS tried to route me to that leg’s starting point again. As for it taking you the most RV friendly route, I’d say no it doesn’t. A lot of my trip was spent on hilly winding roads with steep climbs and sharp curves. My trips set for 6 hours usually took around 9-12 hours because the trip planner obviously doesn’t take into account the speed that you’ve set (mine was 55 mph as a first time towing) but the actual speed limit of the area. 100% this app is not worth paying for.

reviews.title: Inaccurate and not very reliable - be careful if you use
reviews.text:
Inaccurate park information and poor search capabilities. The search field indicates you can enter and search by a park name, location, city, etc. but specific cities/locations are not returned unless there is a specific place to stay located there. It takes additional steps to find locations in the vicinity of a city (Seattle - not exactly a small place) and many sites have been out of business for years or have specific requirements to stay that are NOT mentioned anywhere: i.e. to stay you must be a VFW or Elks Club or military member, etc.
We contacted their customer service who indicated that users are entirely responsible for adding places to stay or reporting them closed.  RV life verifies NOTHING. 
Upgrading to their paid RV Pro doesn’t give more accurate access.
